pages: The derivative measures the rate of change of a function.
It is the gradient of the tangent to the curve at a point.
If y = x^n, then dy/dx = n x^(n-1).
The derivative of a constant is zero.
Product rule: d(uv)/dx = u dv/dx + v du/dx.
Chain rule: dy/dx = dy/du times du/dx.
At a stationary point the derivative is zero.
If the second derivative is positive the point is a minimum; if negative, a maximum.
